sections.bio:
Ex Swiss Super League goalkeeper turned finance entrepreneur: early team member at SwissBorg (crypto unicorn), now co-founder of Vemo (independent, fee-only investment advisory) and Propit (real estate investments). I write about investing, entrepreneurship, business and building companies in Switzerland, in plain language, backed by real client cases.

My audience: 13K followers, 53% engagement: Swiss-based professionals, investors, founders and expats who take financial decisions seriously. 13% are founders/C-level.

What I create: Educational posts, personal storytelling, product deep-dives and honest pov. I only promote products I’d use with my own clients, that’s why my audience trusts a recommendation.

Looking for: Long-term partnerships with fintech, banking, crypto and real estate brands targeting the Swiss/DACH market. Sponsored posts, product launches, ambassador deals.

posts.text:
Which Swiss company started where?

8.8 million people. Probably more global brands per capita than any country on earth. 🇨🇭

Which company is missing here?

Never invest in something you don’t understand. Yet most investors don’t understand the one thing silently eating up their returns:

Hidden fees.

Here’s what your insurance/bank doesn’t want you to know:

→ The average fund charges 1.4% TER, that’s 10x what you’d pay with index alternatives.

→ Retrocessions are still being pocketed by “advisors” who claim to work for you.

→ Your pension fund likely underperforms a simple global ETF by 1-2% annually.

→ Over 30 years, a 1.5% fee difference turns CHF 500K into CHF 300K less wealth.

→ “Active management” beats the benchmark less than 15% of the time.

→ Your advisor’s “free” consultation is paid for by the products they sell you.

→ Currency hedging fees, transaction costs, and custody fees are buried in the fine print.

Warren Buffett has said it for decades: fees are the silent killer of returns.

The old school financial industry benefits heavily if you never do this math. So they hope you simply never do it. Do it. 

Cheers 🥂

I just let Claude Cowork analyze all my LinkedIn posts from the past 12 months. The results? Brutally honest. And honestly… kind of humbling.

Here's what I learned:
📊 My Finance & Investing posts crush everything else. One single post comparing Cisco's dot-com crash to NVIDIA hit 95K impressions. That's 19x my average. Turns out: people love a good "history repeats itself" chart more than Monday motivation.

🪙 Crypto & Bitcoin content has a loyal community. SwissBorg posts, macro correlations, Bitcoin takes: they don't always go viral but the engagement is insane. My crypto people show up every time.

🎭 Personal stories beat generic motivation 3:1. The post about me thinking off getting my own mortgage at PostFinance after negotiating them for others? 6.5K impressions. "Success isn't about speed, it's about direction"? 860. Ouch.

😂 Humor works. But I barely use it. Only 2 humor posts in 12 months and they outperform most of my "serious" content. Note to self: be funnier. lol

📉 Event announcements are basically invisible. Average 425 impressions. Nobody cares about your event until you tell them what they MISSED at the event.

The biggest takeaway?
I don't conform to typical LinkedIn standards. Never have. But the data shows that when I combine real stories with actual numbers and a bit of personality… that's when LinkedIn actually works.

Less templates. More truth.
What about you, do you know which of your posts actually perform? You might be surprised. Cheers 🥂
